what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat serious fungal infections, including a type called invasive aspergillosis (a lung infection caused by a mold) and invasive mucormycosis (another serious mold infection). It works by stopping the fungus from growing and spreading in your body.
how_to_take: Isavuconazonium comes as a capsule to swallow by mouth or as an injection given by a healthcare provider in a clinic or hospital. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush, chew, dissolve, or open them. You can take this medicine with or without food. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: For most adults, the usual starting dose is 2 capsules (372 mg total) taken three times a day, 8 hours apart, for the first 2 days (this is called the loading dose). After that, the usual maintenance dose is 2 capsules once daily. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions, as your dose may be different depending on your situation.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is within 8 hours of the time you were supposed to take it. If more than 8 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double up or take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store the capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Store in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use capsules past the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking this medicine with ketoconazole or high-dose ritonavir, as the combination can be dangerous. Do not take rifampin, rifabutin, carbamazepine, St. John's Wort, or long-acting barbiturates (like phenobarbital) while on this medicine, as they can make isavuconazonium less effective. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, as this drug can interact with many medications including blood thinners, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, and sirolimus. Avoid drinking alcohol. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or confused.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual tiredness, fast or irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath, chest pain, severe skin rash or blistering, swelling of your face, lips, or throat, signs of low potassium (muscle cramps, weakness), or any worsening symptoms. Also tell your doctor if you have liver problems, as your liver will need to be monitored during treatment.
when_it_works: Isavuconazonium starts working fairly quickly, but it may take several days to weeks before you feel a noticeable improvement. Fungal infections can be serious and slow to respond, so it is very important to take every dose and complete your full course of treatment even if you start feeling better. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnant women should avoid this medicine unless absolutely necessary, as it may harm the unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 28 days after the last dose. Breastfeeding mothers should talk to their doctor before taking this medicine. This medicine is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age. People with severe liver disease (Child-Pugh Class C) should not take this medicine. Older adults (65 years and older) can generally take the same dose but should be monitored closely by their doctor.
